summary.what_changed: Added three process rules to CLAUDE.md distilled from the CCE-170/171/172/173 work cycle: (1) before removing accidental persistence, verify nothing depends on it as a de facto data archive; (2) detection shipped as a stand-in for a withdrawn fix must ship with an explicit exit criterion (threshold + date) in the same PR; (3) a metric read from a nonexistent schema key looks identical to a genuine zero, so counts must be verified against the object's real keys and measured absences must be paired with a positive control. No code changes — CLAUDE.md only.
summary.why: Each rule was extracted from a concrete cost incurred during the CCE-170–173 cycle: deleting a mistakenly-committed file destroyed the only durable archive of CCE-141 diagnostic firings (dependency on a side effect rather than an interface); a detection-only diagnostic shipped without a stopping condition left an unanswerable 'do we have data yet?' after three weeks; and a probe for a field that never existed in the schema silently reported a fake zero. Capturing them as standing rules prevents the same class of mistake recurring in future cycles.

summary.what_changed: Documents root-cause diagnosis of a 23-day docs-publishing freeze in the engineering-docs-agent nightly pipeline: every run since 2026-08-22 opens a PR, reports partial, and leaves last_successful_run unchanged. Six consecutive nights show three different proximate content failures (lint_block, schema_invalid, time_budget_exceeded) all collapsing into the same structural outcome (held_back_no_advance_no_cursor / auto_merge_skipped: partial_run). The analysis traces this to CCE-140's deferral-skip safety valve: its deferral_counts counter only persists to state.json on a merged PR branch, but a partial run never merges, so the counter can never reach its 3-strike threshold and the release valve can never fire. Evidence includes byte-identical deferral_counts across 23 days/~23 runs. No fix is attempted — the PR is analysis-only, captured as a doc because claude-mem capture was down at diagnosis time.
summary.why: A prior related stall (CCE-152) was already fixed in main and predates every failing night, so this is a new, structurally distinct recurrence that needed independent root-causing before any repair could be proposed. The finding needed to be recorded durably (as a doc rather than session memory) so the interchangeable-trigger insight — fixing any single content failure won't fix the stall — isn't lost before a follow-up fix is scoped.

doc_targets.notes: Incident/root-cause postmortem; core lens has no archive/operations section yet, so filed as a flat dated slug at lens root per convention. Analysis-only PR — no code fix landed, so no architecture edit is implicated.

summary.what_changed: Corrects three false claims in the CCE-175 handoff investigation doc that were caused by a flawed diff methodology (a silently-failed `git fetch` left `FETCH_HEAD` pointing at `origin/main`, so the comparison was `main` vs `main` and trivially 'equal'). Using `gh pr diff` against the actual nightly PR instead, the corrected doc shows: the deferral counter does increment (fifteen entries per run, not stuck), merge-as-promotion is dead only for blind runs (not degraded ones), and the ~132-line diff is real content, not formatting churn. This reverses the prior recommendation — manually merging a degraded nightly persists counters without advancing the watermark past undocumented work, so a couple of merged nightlies could arm the threshold with no real code change. The doc now instructs verifying `last_successful_run.head_sha` is unchanged before each manual merge, and replaces a retracted 'unstable serializer' theory with a general warning: resolve PR refs explicitly and never pipe a fetch failure to `/dev/null`.
summary.why: The original CCE-175 handoff doc was merged an hour earlier (#250) with a diff comparison that silently used the wrong git ref, producing a tautological result and three incorrect conclusions. This PR corrects the doc before the next session acts on the false claims, and confirms the original CCE-175 root cause is not superseded.
